name: Disclosure (Show/Hide)
description: A button that controls the visibility of a section of content; toggling it shows or hides the associated content.

raweb_criteria.reason: The button's expanded/collapsed state must be exposed via aria-expanded — a visual chevron alone tells assistive technologies nothing.
The control must be a real button so Enter and Space work without a keydown handler.
The trigger must show a visible focus indicator.
Collapsed content must be genuinely hidden from assistive technologies. Hiding it with opacity or visual clipping alone leaves it readable and tabbable while invisible.

keyboard_interactions.action: Toggles the visibility of the disclosure content
Toggles the visibility of the disclosure content

roles.description: Identifies the control element as a button. Implicit on `<button>` — do not add it manually.

required_attributes.description: State. Goes on the BUTTON, never on the panel: it describes what the button does, not what the panel is.

optional_attributes.description: References the id of the controlled panel. Support is thin — treat it as a bonus, never as the thing that conveys state. The panel must always exist in the DOM for the reference to resolve.

notes: Prefer native `<details>`/`<summary>`: the browser supplies the button semantics, aria-expanded, Enter/Space, and the show/hide behaviour with zero JS.
aria-expanded belongs on the control, not the panel — this is the single most common disclosure bug.

Hide the panel with the `hidden` attribute or `display: none`. Never with `opacity: 0`, `visibility: hidden` + `height: 0`, or off-screen positioning: those leave the content in the accessibility tree and in the tab order.

Do not toggle the button's accessible name (Show/Hide) AND aria-expanded — a screen reader then announces the state twice, and contradictorily. Keep the name stable and let aria-expanded carry the state.
The disclosure pattern is simpler than accordion — use it for standalone show/hide controls
